new_jobs.description:
Our world is transforming, and PTC is leading the way. Our software brings the physical and digital worlds together, enabling companies to improve operations, create better products, and empower people in all aspects of their business.

Our people make all the difference in our success. Today, we are a global team of nearly 7,000 and our main objective is to create opportunities for our team members to explore, learn, and grow – all while seeing their ideas come to life and celebrating the differences that make us who we are and the work we do possible.

Senior AI Software Engineer

PTC’s software is used to design, build and service many of the world’s most complex products, from aircraft and cars to medical devices and industrial equipment. We’re bringing AI into that portfolio, and we’re looking for engineers who want to build AI that holds up in demanding, real-world environments.

As a Senior AI Software Engineer, you will build these systems and take them from prototype to production. You will work in a small, fast-moving squad, with engineers, product managers and designers, shipping agentic features that real customers use.

Key Responsibilities

Build AI agents and the services around them, using LLMs, retrieval and agentic workflows, and connect them to PTC's products, data and APIs.
Make agents production grade: state that survives restarts, long running work that pauses for human input and resumes, tool permissions scoped to each user, and defenses against prompt injection.
Develop the APIs, tools and integrations, including MCP servers, that let agents act on enterprise systems safely.
Build eval suites and automated tests that catch regressions as models, prompts and data change, and use them as release gates.
Instrument services with metrics, monitoring and tracing for quality, latency and cost, and use that data to improve the system in production.
Ship continuously and own what you ship, from design through deployment, including participating in an on-call rotation for the services your team runs.
Raise the bar for the team through code review, design discussions and mentoring, working with security, architecture and engineering colleagues across PTC's global organization.

Qualifications

5+ years of software engineering, including building and running distributed services or SaaS applications.
Experience shipping at least one LLM-based feature (an agent, a RAG system or an AI workflow) to production users, not just prototypes.
Strong skills in at least one of Python, Java, TypeScript or C++.
Solid fundamentals: software design, APIs, data structures, automated testing and modern development practices.
Experience with cloud-native development on Azure, AWS or GCP: containers, Kubernetes and CI/CD.
Experience integrating AI models with application logic, enterprise data and external tools.
Sound judgment on technical trade-offs, and ownership of features from design through production support.
Clear communication and experience working with distributed teams
A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

Nice to have

Experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain, and with MCP.
Experience with vector search, embeddings and retrieval pipelines over enterprise knowledge.
Experience with AI evaluation frameworks, LLMOps and observability tools (for example Datadog).
Experience in enterprise software, CAD, PLM (product lifecycle management), ALM (application lifecycle management), SLM (service lifecycle management), industrial software or a related domain.

This position is not eligible for employment-based immigration sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring current or future sponsorship from PTC.

The salary range reflects a good-faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate's skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Additionally, candidates may be eligible for a performance-based bonus. Certain roles may also be eligible for participation in our equity programs. Employees may be eligible for medical, dental and vision insurance, paid time off and sick leave, tuition reimbursement, 401(k) contributions and employer match, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, disability coverage and, if you are an office-assigned employee, a generous commuter subsidy. All total rewards and benefits programs are

subject to applicable plan eligibility and other terms and conditions.

For more information about PTC’s comprehensive benefits, please visit our Careers Page.

Applications will be accepted on an on-going basis.

At PTC, we believe in the power of diverse ideas and perspectives. As a global company that values and respects all identities, cultures, and perspectives, we strive to create an inclusive PTC for ALL through an environment where everyone feels like they belong and are empowered to bring their true, authentic selves to work. Proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, ethnicity, ancestry, marital status, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations. PTC endeavors to make ptc.com/careers accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding the accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process, please contact PTC's Talent Acquisition team at TalentAcquisition@ptc.com. This contact information is for accommodation requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.

Life at PTC is about more than working with today’s most cutting-edge technologies to transform the physical world. It’s about showing up as you are and working alongside some of today’s most talented industry leaders to transform the world around you.

If you share our passion for problem-solving through innovation, you’ll likely become just as passionate about the PTC experience as we are. Are you ready to explore your next career move with us?

Job Description

Position Summary

We aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. We're at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals. The Cyber Applied AI team is looking for a Senior Data Scientist to build detection and investigation analytics over enterprise security data. The work is statistical: finding unusual behavior in very high-volume network and endpoint telemetry, measuring similarity between security events, correlating alerts from multiple sources into unified incidents mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, and turning threat intelligence into structured, usable data. The person in this role takes an analytical method from idea through validation and into production, and owns the data pipelines that feed it.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a data scientist who also engineers. The person in it designs the method, builds the pipelines and services that run it, deploys it on Azure or AWS, and keeps it in production. That includes applied AI work: building AI-driven analysis systems that use Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools over security data stores to automate investigation and shorten triage, and exposing results through APIs and automated reporting.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain statistical anomaly detection over network telemetry at the scale of billions of records per day, using behavioral baselines, percentile thresholds (p95/p99), new and rare entity detection, and feature engineering.
Design correlation frameworks that use IDF weighting, entity similarity metrics, and MITRE ATT&CK mappings to aggregate EDR and other security telemetry into unified security events.
Implement these methods as production workflows in Azure Data Explorer using KQL functions and materialized views.
Evaluate detection and correlation methods with defined metrics (precision, recall, false positive rate, time to triage), validate them against labeled incidents and analyst feedback, and monitor for drift once in production.
Build pipelines that extract CVEs, indicators of compromise, and other structured intelligence from unstructured sources such as security news and vendor reporting.
Design AI-driven security analysis systems that use MCP tools against Azure Data Explorer and threat intelligence services to automate investigations and reduce triage time.
Turn analytical methods into repeatable detection and investigation workflows with automated reporting.
Design and operate the data pipelines that feed the analytics, including batch and streaming ingestion on AWS (S3, Lambda, Glue, Step Functions, Kinesis) and Azure.
Write ETL/ELT transformations in Spark and Python for large cybersecurity datasets.
Identify where a purpose-built analytical system can replace a commercial product and build it when the economics justify it.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
At least 5 years building statistical or machine learning methods and engineering them into production systems, including the data pipelines, cloud services, and APIs around them.
Hands-on experience with statistical anomaly detection, behavioral baselining, or similarity-based correlation on datasets in the hundreds of millions of records or larger.
Experience with security telemetry (network, endpoint/EDR, cloud, or identity) and familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Strong Python and SQL. Working experience with an analytics query language such as KQL and with Spark or PySpark.
At least 3 years building data pipelines on Azure or AWS, including both batch and streaming ingestion.
Able to explain a method and its limits to engineers, analysts, and managers.

Preferred

Master's degree in data science, Statistics, Physics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field and at least 5 years of experience
Production experience with Azure Data Explorer, KQL functions, and materialized views.
Experience extracting structured intelligence (CVEs, IOCs) from unstructured text.
Experience building AI-driven analysis systems with LLM applications, AI agents, or MCP tools (for example Microsoft Foundry) over security data.
Experience with AWS data lake tooling: S3, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions, Kinesis.
Computer vision or deep learning work with PyTorch.
A record of replacing a commercial tool with an in-house analytical solution and measuring the savings.
Experience in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or another regulated industry.

Required Skills

Business Intelligence (BI), Database Design, Data Engineering, Data Modeling, Data Science, Data Visualization, Machine Learning (ML), Software Development, Stakeholder Relationship Management, Waterfall Model

Description

UC San Diego Health is on a journey to build and mature enterprise applied artificial intelligence capabilities that deliver meaningful, measurable impact at scale across the health system. This work reflects a sustained organizational commitment to developing these capabilities as a core part of how care is delivered and supported. The purpose of UCSDH’s applied AI efforts is grounded in the quadruple aim, using AI-enabled technologies to simultaneously expand access to care, improve clinical and operational outcomes, enhance quality and safety, and support a better experience for both patients and care teams. A key focus is leveraging real-time data, predictive, generative, and hybrid models, and increasingly automated interventions to demonstrably achieve impact at scale across the health system.

Central to this strategy is the Mission Control vision, which brings together real-time data and applied AI–driven decision support to provide system-wide insight and action across the care continuum, including population health. This initiative serves both as a delivery layer for targeted point solutions across the health system and as a centralized hub for system-level assessment, prediction, and coordinated action. The supporting technology landscape is intentionally dynamic, with an emphasis on identifying best-fit solutions over time while scaling a cohesive enterprise platform that integrates complementary tools and capabilities.

This position operates within the Jacobs Center for Health Innovation and is integrated into UC San Diego Health Information Services, sharing leadership, data, and infrastructure, while driving translational innovation and supporting enterprise operations at scale.

Position And Team

UC San Diego Health is seeking a Senior Data Scientist to work within the Joan & Irwin Jacobs Center for Health Innovation (JCHI) on all phases of AI model design and development. The role is responsible for the full model lifecycle, including intake and review, data preparation, model development, evaluation, pre-deployment preparation, deployment, and post-deployment model monitoring and management. This includes applying advanced statistical and machine learning methods, causal inference, and experimental design to ensure models not only predict outcomes but drive measurable impact through real-world interventions.

The position operates within a multidisciplinary environment that includes cloud engineers, product managers, AI/automation engineers, application developers, architects, and enterprise platform teams. The Senior Data Scientist owns technical execution across the model lifecycle while partnering closely with product managers who drive product strategy, prioritization, and stakeholder alignment. The position reports to the JCHI Co-Director, who provides functional leadership for data science and AI initiatives and works across JCHI and Information Services stakeholders to align priorities, capabilities, and delivery.

This is a senior technical role that requires the ability to independently lead complex data science projects, mentor junior team members, and contribute to the strategic direction of the data science program. The role involves close collaboration with clinical and operational stakeholders to identify high-impact use cases, translate clinical questions into data science problems, and deliver AI solutions that create sustained value across the health system. This includes working across diverse data modalities (e.g., structured EHR data, time-series, imaging, and unstructured text) and leveraging state-of-the-art approaches, including predictive, generative, and hybrid models.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate brings deep experience across the full AI model lifecycle in healthcare or complex enterprise environments, with demonstrated ability to independently lead projects from data exploration through production deployment and ongoing monitoring. Experience with healthcare EHR data, particularly Epic, is essential, and candidates should be comfortable working with complex, multimodal clinical datasets to develop models that drive measurable improvements in patient care and health system operations at scale.

Experience developing AI models using traditional machine learning, large language models, and hybrid approaches is strongly desired, including familiarity with cloud-based data science platforms such as AWS and modern ML infrastructure. Candidates should be highly proficient in Python, R, SQL, and related tools, with strong expertise in model evaluation, benchmarking, and performance optimization, as well as applying rigorous methods to ensure robustness, generalizability, and real-world impact.

Successful candidates will also demonstrate strong familiarity with enterprise health system operations and technologies, including electronic health records, healthcare data integration, and cloud platforms, along with the regulatory and privacy considerations unique to healthcare AI. The role requires the ability to work effectively across clinical, operational, technical, and vendor stakeholders, and to contribute to data science strategy in environments where innovation, scientific rigor, and patient safety must coexist.

Nine (9) years of related experience, education/training, OR a Bachelor’s degree in related area plus five (5) years of related experience/training. Related experience includes data science, computational science, machine learning, AI model development, and work with healthcare EHR data (e.g., Epic).
Advanced knowledge of HPC / data science / CI.

In depth experience assessing a broad spectrum of technical and research needs and demands and establish priorities, delegate and / or lead development of solutions to meet such needs.
Demonstrated advanced experience in one or more of the following: optimizing, benchmarking, HPC performance and power modeling, analyzing hardware, software, and applications for HPC / data / CI.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong data science discipline across the full AI model lifecycle (intake, data prep, model development, evaluation, deployment, monitoring). Demonstrated ability to lead complex data science research projects with multi-institutional scope and serve as technical lead.

new_jobs.description:
About Carpe & the Role

Carpe is an AI-native company building platforms and data products that help P&C insurance carriers make better decisions. At Carpe, we don’t hand-write code anymore. We build with AI. As a Senior AI Software Engineer, you will turn business needs and prototypes into reliable production systems by directing frontier models and coding agents, shaping the environments they work in, and verifying what they deliver. AI is your primary way of building—not an autocomplete tool added to a traditional coding workflow. You bring extensive hands-on experience with frontier models, agents, and agent harnesses, plus the engineering judgment to take their work all the way through AWS deployment and production operation.

You’ll have a say in how we build. Our design and architecture patterns give you a solid starting point, not a set of limits. If a new approach or technology will better serve our customers, make the case. We care far more about how you think through tradeoffs than whether you’ve used every tool we use.

Responsibilities

Turn business needs into executable work.
Partner with Product to define the problem, constraints, acceptance criteria, and customer outcome. Give agents the specifications, repository context, examples, and verification steps they need to deliver the right solution; resolve ambiguity before it becomes working software that solves the wrong problem.
Architect systems and direct AI delivery.
Break complex work into bounded tasks, choose interfaces and data flows, and direct agents through implementation, integration, and debugging. Use our approved patterns to address scale, latency, reliability, and data correctness across products. You own the architecture and outcome, even when AI produces the code.
Build effective agent workflows and harnesses.
Scope and steer bots through our team workflow, including Slack and Linear. Configure the context, tools, permissions, execution environments, and feedback loops around agents; manage handoffs, checkpoints, and recovery when they stall or go off course. Run a tight build-and-verify loop: the agent builds, you exercise the result in a live test environment, feed back precise findings, and repeat until the acceptance criteria are met.
Choose models and approaches deliberately.
Evaluate frontier models and coding agents on real engineering tasks, comparing output quality, reliability, context handling, latency, and cost. Match the model and harness to the work, and adapt as capabilities change. Let customer outcomes, not tool loyalty, guide decisions.
Prove the result, not the agent’s claim.
Review architecture and generated changes at the level the risk demands; personally inspect sensitive changes. Use independent checks, representative data, automated tests, regression checks, and end-to-end behavior to catch plausible-but-wrong output. Where systems use models at runtime, evaluate their behavior and failure modes too.
Ship and operate in AWS.
Take AI-built software through cloud deployment and production support with QA and DevOps. Direct and verify infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD changes; understand access controls, secrets, networking, data storage, rollout, and rollback. Use logs, metrics, and traces to diagnose failures, verify recovery, and own incident follow-through—including failures introduced by agents.
Make the next AI build better.
Turn successful approaches and failures into reusable agent instructions, repository guidance, harness improvements, and verification routines. Keep architecture and operational context current so both people and agents can build on it.

What we are looking for

7+ years of professional software engineering, delivering and supporting production systems (overall experience, not five years with today’s AI tools).
Extensive frontier-model experience.
Substantial use of frontier models across multiple model families—for example, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini—in real software delivery. You can explain which models you choose for planning, implementation, debugging, and review; where they fail; and how you evaluate a new release. You actively experiment and clearly prefer building with AI over a hand-coding-first workflow.
Extensive agent and harness experience
. You have shipped meaningful work with coding agents and agent harnesses—not just chat prompts or autocomplete. Examples may include Claude Code, Codex, other agentic development environments, or custom harnesses. Extra credit for OpenClaw. You can configure repository instructions, context and tool access, isolated execution, task decomposition, verification, and recovery, and explain when orchestration helps versus adding overhead.
End-to-end systems ownership.
You have personally designed a complete system through professional or substantial independent work, with relevant professional experience around similar systems. Show how you directed AI from an initial specification through a working, deployed result, what you personally decided, and how you established that it worked. You don’t need to have led a large-system initiative.
Engineering depth behind the agents.
Strong programming, debugging, architecture, and systems reasoning. You can read and interrogate generated code, trace data flows and service interactions, identify flawed assumptions, and steer a correction. We value your ability to make AI-built systems correct and maintainable—not the volume of code you type.
AWS and cloud deployment experience.
You have deployed and supported production software in AWS and understand the path from repository to running service: infrastructure as code, CI/CD, compute or containers, storage, networking, IAM, secrets, observability, and rollback. Explain a deployment or incident you owned and how you verified the outcome.
Roll-up-your-sleeves, low-ego collaboration
. Comfortable steering agents, investigating failures, explaining tradeoffs, and influencing without direct authority in a small. Share work and blockers openly, move across products, and help teammates improve their AI workflows while staying accountable for the customer outcome.

Why Carpe?

Your work shows up fast. At our size, what you build reaches customers quickly, and you quickly make an impact
Growth: We have a clear growth framework with defined levels and competencies, so you always know what's expected and what "next" looks like.
Collaboration: Work with teams in sales, marketing, engineering, product, and customer success.

new_jobs.title: Founding ML Platform Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About Parisi Labs

Parisi Labs is building foundational world models for physical industry. We are developing models that learn how complex physical systems behave and reuse that understanding across forecasts, scenarios, and operational decisions.

Energy is our first proving ground. We combine historical and live data with operational context, bringing together machine learning research, data infrastructure, and software engineering to turn advances in modeling into useful technology for energy operators.

We are a small technical team working directly with the founders on our core models, systems, and products.

About The Role

We are looking for a Founding ML Platform Engineer to design, build, and own the infrastructure that takes our machine learning models from research into reliable production systems.

You will establish the core MLOps platform at Parisi Labs, creating the tools and workflows that allow researchers to operationalize models without becoming responsible for the infrastructure around them. This includes model registries, dataset and experiment lineage, retraining workflows, scheduled batch inference, and production monitoring.

Our models operate on complex, time-dependent data, producing forecasts and simulations of physical systems. You will build the infrastructure that makes these workflows reproducible, observable, and dependable as our research and products evolve.

This is a hands-on founding engineering role with significant technical ownership. You will work directly with our CTO, Chief Scientist, and researchers to define the platform architecture, select technologies, and implement the systems the company will build on.

What You'll Own

Design and build our end-to-end MLOps platform, from model registration and versioning through deployment, inference, and monitoring.
Develop reliable, scalable batch inference infrastructure for recurring forecasts and model-generated simulations.
Build model registries and lineage systems that track training inputs, dataset versions, model configurations, artifacts, and deployment history.
Create standardized workflows and tools that allow researchers to register models, manage experiments, and move models into production.
Develop automated retraining and deployment pipelines, including dataset preparation, validation, version promotion, and rollback.
Build monitoring and observability for model performance, forecast accuracy, data drift, pipeline health, and production failures.
Help steer the technical and research direction of the company.

What we're looking for

6+ years of software engineering experience, including significant hands-on experience building and operating production ML systems.
A track record of designing and owning ML infrastructure or MLOps platforms, ideally having built systems from the ground up.
Strong Python and backend engineering skills, with experience building reliable data processing and distributed workflow systems.
Experience with ML lifecycle tooling such as MLflow, orchestration frameworks such as Dagster, Airflow, or Prefect, and modern cloud infrastructure.
Deep familiarity with model deployment, batch inference, model versioning, data lineage, and production monitoring.
Comfort working closely with ML researchers and translating experimental workflows into reliable engineering systems.
An entrepreneurial mindset, strong technical ownership, and the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving environment with limited structure.

Especially compelling backgrounds:

Experience as a founder, technical co-founder, or founding engineer at an early-stage startup.
Experience building an ML platform from zero to production, rather than exclusively maintaining established infrastructure.
Experience as an early technical hire who helped establish engineering architecture, tooling, and practices.
Experience with time-series forecasting, energy systems, or other data-intensive scientific applications.

First 90 days

30 days: Understand our research workflows, existing model infrastructure, and production forecasting systems. Identify the most important gaps in model lifecycle management, serving, and observability.
60 days: Establish foundational model registry and lineage capabilities, and deliver an initial standardized workflow for moving research models into production.
90 days: Own a reliable end-to-end production ML workflow, including model versioning, scheduled inference, monitoring, and clear operational visibility.

Why join

You will establish the platform that all of our models run on. Your work will determine how our research becomes reliable, scalable technology used to support real-world decisions.

As an early engineering hire, you will have substantial ownership over our infrastructure, architecture, and engineering practices, working directly with the founders and researchers developing our core technology.

Location and compensation

Location:
New York City. This is an in-person role.

Salary range:
$200,000–$280,000 USD.

Equity
: meaningful early-company equity.

Our team owns the foundational AI/GenAI platform services that power CVS Health's internal agentic and LLM-driven tooling — including LLM routing and cost governance infrastructure, internal developer tooling for AI-assisted software development, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities, and orchestration tools for building and deploying agentic workflows. Experience with observability/telemetry tooling (e.g., OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Langfuse, Datadog)

new_jobs.title: Senior Research Scientist - HPC & AI
new_jobs.description:
Requisition Id 17454

Overview

The Analytics and AI methods at Scale (AAIMS) group in the National Center for Computational Science (NCCS) is hiring Senior Research Scientist to push the frontier of AI for science such as: scientific reasoning, federated & collaborative learning, and reinforcement learning (RL) for self-improving models on leadership-class supercomputers. You’ll help design, train, and evaluate AI systems that plan, reason, and take actions to accelerate discovery across domains (materials, chemistry, climate, fusion, biology, and more).

NCCS operates the Frontier exascale supercomputer and world-class data facilities. This role sits at the intersection of AI at scale and HPC, giving you unmatched resources to prototype new ideas, run large ablations, and translate methods into scientific impact.

Examples Of Focus Areas

Agentic AI for Science: Autonomous and tool-using agents for experiment design, simulation steering, data collection, and lab/compute orchestration; planning and memory; multi-agent collaboration.
Scientific Reasoning: Program/path-of-thought, tool-augmented and retrieval-augmented reasoning; uncertainty quantification and calibrated decisions.
RL & Self-Improving Models: RLHF/RLAIF, online RL, self-play, open-ended discovery, reward modeling, curriculum/active learning, data selection, iterative post-training, safety alignment and guardrails.
Foundation Models for Science @ Scale: Pretraining, instruction tuning, continued pretraining, Mixture-of-Experts; distributed training/inference (FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, tensor/sequence parallelism); scalable evaluation pipelines for reasoning and agents.
Federated & Collaborative Learning: Cross-silo training across institutions and facilities; privacy-preserving learning (secure aggregation, differential privacy, MPC/HE); personalization under heterogeneity; governance-aware data/model sharing; collaborative evaluation.

The NCCS is the home of the world’s first exascale supercomputer Frontier. Our Leadership Computing Program (OLCF) provides world class computing facilities to applications across all computational domains and disciplines. We are an inclusive dynamic environment that welcomes those with initiative and creativity.

Major Duties/Responsibilities

Develop and coordinate division activities in HPC-AI with cross-cutting initiatives in the laboratory by establishing forward-looking centers of excellence.
Lead and collaborate with internal and external researchers on a variety of extreme-scale AI/ML research and projects.
Lead in authoring peer reviewed papers, technical papers, reports, and proposals. Advance personal and staff contributions in leading professional, academic, and research organizations.
Advance personal and staff contributions in leading professional, academic, and research organizations.
Team Building & Mentorship: Provide mentorship to postdocs, students, and junior staff, fostering long-term career development.
Stakeholder Engagement: Effectively communicate vision, strategy, and progress to DOE sponsors, industrial partners, and international collaborators.

Basic Qualifications

PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a field closely related to the job duties of this position.
A minimum of 6 years of relevant research experience outside of Ph.D.
Demonstrated research in cross-cutting fields of HPC and/or AI.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership in conceiving, planning, and delivering large-scale HPC-AI projects with measurable scientific or technological impact.
Experience securing competitive funding (e.g., DOE, NSF, DARPA, industry consortia) and leading multi-institution proposals.
Recognition by the broader community – invited talks, keynote addresses, professional society awards, or major benchmarks.
Impactful open-source contributions to HPC or AI framework (e.g., Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, Ray, Distributed RL)
Interdisciplinary collaboration experience – working with domain scientist (climate, material, fusion, biology) to translate methods into real discoveries.
Strategic vision – ability to identify long-term research directions at the intersection of AI, HPC and domain sciences.

Special Requirements

For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.
To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.
For foreign national candidates: If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment.

Please submit two letters of reference when applying to this position. You may upload these directly to your application or have them sent to ORNLRecruiting@ornl.gov with the position title and number referenced in the subject line.

Instructions To Upload Documents To Your Candidate Profile

Login to your account via jobs.ornl.gov
View Profile
Under the My Documents section, select Add a Document

About ORNL

As a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science national laboratory, ORNL has an impressive 80-year legacy of addressing the nation’s most pressing challenges. Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment. These principles are essential for supporting our broader mission to drive scientific breakthroughs and translate them into solutions for energy, environmental, and security challenges facing the nation.

ORNL offers competitive pay and benefits programs to attract and retain individuals who demonstrate exceptional work behaviors. The laboratory provides a range of employee benefits, including medical and retirement plans and flexible work hours, to support the well-being of you and your family. Employee amenities such as on-site fitness, banking, and cafeteria facilities are also available for added convenience.

Other benefits include the following: Prescription Drug Plan, Dental Plan, Vision Plan, 401(k) Retirement Plan, Contributory Pension Plan, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Generous Vacation and Holidays, Parental Leave, Legal Insurance with Identity Theft Protection, Employee Assistance Plan, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, Wellness Programs, Educational Assistance, Relocation Assistance, and Employee Discounts.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Applied AI Engineer — Global Health & AI

ICF's Global Health and Development (GHD) line of business, part of the Health, People, and Human Services (HPHS) Group, is seeking an Applied AI Engineer
to build frontier-model systems for various global health and survey programs. This role will support the development of AI-enabled tools that draft survey reports, let researchers and policymakers analyze data in natural language, translate questionnaires into low-resource languages, and support interviewers and data quality in the field. No tool is adopted unless it matches or beats the expert-led process it replaces. You will build the prompting, agent, and pipeline layer across the program. You will also build the evaluation harnesses that show whether each tool actually works, judged against ground truth produced by some of the most experienced survey methodologists in the world.

This position can be remote within the United States, with occasional travel.

It is contingent upon award of program funding.

Key Responsibilities

Design and build LLM pipelines and agents for survey workflows, including:
an AI-assisted data-to-report pipeline
natural-language analysis of survey data
multilingual questionnaire translation
field support tools for interviewers and supervisors

Build evaluation harnesses as first-class deliverables. Work with the Technical Lead and survey experts to define acceptance criteria before the work is judged. Build test sets from expert-produced ground truth and run the non-inferiority comparisons that decide whether a tool moves forward.
Route work across models based on reasoning complexity, volume, cost, latency, and data-residency requirements.
Manage inference cost by tracking token usage, context limits, prompt caching, and batch processing, and account for these operating costs in model-selection decisions.
Connect models to data services and to the applications built by full stack developers.
Use agentic coding tools to produce software from clear specifications, then review, test, and own the resulting code.
Monitor production systems, conduct disciplined error analysis, and report positive and negative results.
Document methods and results for public release, including negative results. Help transfer tools to partner-country institutions so they can run them on their own.

Minimum Required Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent years experience)
Minimum 4 years of professional software development experience, including building LLM-powered systems that real users relied on in production
U.S. citizenship is required by federal government contract

Additional Required Skills And Experience

Proficiency in Python or another modern programming language (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Go) for back-end and AI application development
Hands-on experience building with frontier-model APIs (from any provider, or through any cloud platform), including tool use and retrieval-augmented generation
Demonstrated experience designing LLM evaluations, including test-set construction, automated and human grading, regression testing, and ship/no-ship decisions.
Working knowledge of LLM cost, latency, and model-selection trade-offs
Experience building and deploying on a major cloud platform (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud)
Demonstrated experience using agentic coding tools, such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or GitHub Copilot agent mode, to specify, review, test, and take ownership of production code.
Experience with agent frameworks and AI evaluation tooling.

Preferred Skills

Experience with tasks where ground truth came from subject matter experts (for example, statisticians, clinicians, scientists, or methodologists)
Experience with grounded generation over structured or tabular data, or with LLM-assisted statistical analysis
Experience with multilingual or low-resource-language NLP, translation, or speech
Experience deploying open-weight models
Experience with sensitive or regulated data, such as health data or human-subjects research
Familiarity with model governance, monitoring, and responsible AI practice
Experience in global health, international development, or low- and middle-income country settings
Public work such as open-source contributions, published evaluations, or technical writing about systems you built undefined

Professional Skills

Explains AI trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including funders, survey experts, and partner-government staff
Collaborates effectively across disciplines, cultures, time zones, and organizational levels while treating domain experts as the source of truth
Communicates uncertainty, limitations, and negative results candidly.Self-motivated
Finds ways to add value without a lot of direct supervision

new_jobs.description:
Company Intro

At Toloka AI
we create data that powers leading GenAI models and innovations. We work with frontier labs, big tech, renowned AI startups, enterprises and non-profit research organizations worldwide. We use a combination of Experts + Crowd + Tech Platform to teach AI models to reason and evaluate their efficacy and safety. We have experts in more than 50 different domains - from doctors and lawyers to physicists and engineers - and boast one of the most diverse global crowds, representing over
100 countries and speaking 40+ languages
. We are a well-funded startup with an enviable portfolio of clients including Anthropic
, Amazon
, Microsoft
, Poolside
, Recraft
, and Shopify
.

Recently, we secured strategic investment led by Bezos Expeditions
and Nebius Group
with participation from Mikhail Parakhin
, CTO of Shopify
and board advisor to leading GenAI companies, who now serves as our Chairman of the Board. Our remote-first team is globally distributed around the world: USA
, UK
, the Netherlands
, Serbia
, and more.

About position

The Freelance Forward Deployed AI Engineer
is Toloka's most senior client-facing technical role. You will partner directly with CTOs, VPs of Engineering and ML, research leaders, and applied AI teams, helping them solve complex AI data challenges and translate ambitious model goals into practical, scalable solutions.

This is a hands-on role
. You will design and build the data-generation
, labeling
, and evaluation pipelines t
hat power the next generation of AI models
. Rather than training the models yourself, you'll help clients identify the right data strategy and own the solution from problem discovery through implementation and delivery.

Beyond delivering client solutions, you'll help shape how Toloka approaches AI solution engineering - establishing best practices, raising the technical bar across engagements, and mentoring Solution Engineers
and Technical Consultants
.

Why this role is different

Every engagement is different. One week you might be designing evaluation pipelines for frontier foundation models, the next helping an enterprise build domain-specific reasoning datasets or synthetic data workflows.

This role sits at the intersection of consulting, engineering, and AI. You'll work directly with some of the world's leading AI companies, helping shape how next-generation models are trained and evaluated.

What you'll do

Executive partnership

Act as the primary technical counterpart to CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and research/engineering leadership.
Lead executive conversations using a structured, answer-first (BLUF) approach.
Manage escalations and expectations with composure and integrity.
Build long-term trusted relationships by recommending evidence-based solutions.

Data strategy & needs diagnosis

Ask excellent questions to uncover the client's real need - the "question behind the question." Understand their model, which metrics they want to move, and how they intend to train or evaluate it.
Draw on a solid understanding of how LLMs are trained and fine-tuned
to have credible conversations with their technical leaders, understand their data strategy, and proactively propose the data
that will solve their problem - with options and rationale ("based on your goal, you likely need this, or this").

Solution engineering & delivery (hands-on)

Design and build the data solutions yourself:
configure data-labeling components and quality controls, develop user interfaces and AI-driven solutions (e.g. agentic systems, RAG, synthetic data generation), and integrate them into automated, multi-stage pipelines
that produce data for AI training and evaluation.
Architect and reason about complex, multi-stage solutions
end to end; run experiments to prove the pipeline delivers data of the required quality and speed; iterate from MVP toward production.
Provide technical leadership across multiple client engagements, establish reusable engineering standards and best practices, and mentor Solution Engineers and Technical Consultants to raise the overall technical bar of the organization.

Commercial ownership

Own delivery end to end
- timelines
, quality
, and scalability
- and the commercial outcome
: Gross Margin and Contribution Margin, with the levers, trade-offs, and next checkpoints named, not just described.
Identify and drive expansion opportunities.

About You

Executive communication.
You can confidently lead conversations with CTOs, VPs, and senior technical stakeholders - clear, concise, structured, persuasive, and calm under pressure.
Strong understanding of modern LLM development.
You understand how modern LLMs are trained, fine-tuned, and evaluated (including SFT, RLHF/RLAIF, DPO/PPO, reward modeling, and LoRA/PEFT). You're comfortable discussing these topics with senior technical stakeholders and translating their goals into effective AI data solutions.
Hands-on solution engineering.
You've designed complex AI solutions, built multi-stage pipelines, and developed AI-driven systems (e.g. agentic workflows, RAG, or synthetic data generation). You're comfortable working in Python (NumPy, Pandas), integrating APIs, and independently prototyping LLM-powered solutions.
Solid software engineering foundations.
You understand version control, testing, MVP thinking, and iterative development. Experience building production software is a strong plus.
Exceptional discovery and problem framing.
You enjoy working through ambiguity, asking the right questions, and translating business or research goals into clear AI data and evaluation strategies.
Seniority and track record.
8+ years delivering complex AI, ML, or data projects end to end, with experience influencing technical direction beyond individual projects. Experience establishing engineering standards, mentoring engineers, or leading cross-functional technical initiatives is highly valued. Experience in top-tier strategy consulting (McKinsey, Bain, BCG) and/or as an applied ML / LLM engineer is a strong advantage.
Ownership mindset.
You take responsibility for outcomes, make thoughtful trade-offs between time, cost, and quality, and are comfortable owning both technical and commercial success.

Nice to have

Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning LLMs and/or building agentic systems (helps you reason about client needs - though the role itself is about building data solutions, not training models).
Advanced degree (MSc/PhD) in AI, CS, or a related field.
Experience in crowdsourcing and/or data-centric AI, and with fast-paced, multi-project delivery for frontier AI clients.

What we can offer

Full-time independent contractor engagement
through the Ontop contractor platform
, either as an individual or through your own company or business entity;
Flexible, fully remote schedule ( 40 hours per week
);
Work at the leading edge of AI development, alongside a dedicated and dynamic team of experts;
Projects with customers that are AI industry leaders and well-known household names;
Friendly community.

To learn how we collect, use, disclose, and store personal data, check out our Privacy Notice.

new_jobs.title: Enterprise AI Architecture Consultant
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Accenture Song Service helps leading brands turn customer interactions into an engine for growth, moving service beyond a cost center to something that builds trust, loyalty, and share of wallet. Our Service practice works end to end: we shape the vision and strategy for the service function and help clients implement and run it, innovate the products and services customers rely on, equip client customer service and customer experience teams with the right technology and talent, and turn customer data into insights that strengthen client’s relationship with their customers.

Service AI & Data puts AI at the heart of this work. We help clients reinvent how they serve their customers and support their people: conversational AI and AI agents that resolve customer needs across voice, chat, and messaging; copilots that help service agents and field teams do their best work; and the data foundations, data lakes, reporting, and analytics agents that turn every interaction into insight. The strategies we shape and the experiences we design are delivered into production at enterprise scale.

Who You Are

You are a Forward Deployed Engineer who brings an architectural perspective to integrating AI across complex enterprise systems. You embed directly with clients to connect AI components and cooperating AI agents with the platforms customer service runs on (CRM, contact center, knowledge, telephony, and data), and you build the integrations and reusable patterns that let AI scale across a client's service ecosystem.

You are a builder who is just as comfortable in a client workshop as in a code editor. You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, moving between engagements, picking up new platforms quickly, and explaining technical choices in plain language to engineers and business stakeholders alike. Above all, you are a curious, collaborative teammate who makes the people around you better.

The Work

Embed with client teams, on site and remote, to understand how their service operation really works, from contact center and agent workflows to the systems and data behind them.
Join discovery workshops with client business and technology teams, helping identify, size, and prioritize the AI use cases with the highest impact on customers and the business.
Build rapid prototypes that prove how AI agents can plug into a client's service ecosystem, often within days, before a full build begins.
Design and build integrations that connect AI agents to CRM, contact center, knowledge management, ticketing, telephony, and enterprise data platforms through APIs, events, platform-native connectors, and tool-use patterns such as MCP.
Design how multiple AI agents coordinate across systems, including which agent owns which task, which systems each one can access, and how requests are routed between them.
Map and build the data flows between platforms, so customer, order, case, and interaction data move reliably and securely between AI agents and the systems of record.
Connect AI agents to systems through event-driven patterns, so they can react in real time to moments like a delayed order, a failed payment, or an escalated case.
Build the human handoff and escalation flows that pass full customer context from AI agents to human agents across voice, chat, and messaging.
Carry customer identity and context across channels, so a customer who starts in chat and moves to voice never has to start over, whether they are talking to an AI agent or a person.
Harden integrations for production with testing, logging, observability, and CI/CD, and document integration specifications, reference architectures, and reusable patterns for the wider team.
Bring conversation designs, customer experience journeys, and prototypes to life in code, flagging technical constraints early and iterating quickly as designs evolve and as real usage data comes in.
Support production rollout and adoption: write runbooks, train client teams on new AI-powered workflows, and help deliver a clean handoff to client or managed-delivery teams.
Use AI-assisted engineering tools every day across story grooming, solutioning, testing and triage, and development to raise the speed and quality of delivery.
Contribute reusable components, accelerators, and lessons learned from the field so our teams deliver faster on the next engagement.
Help onboard and mentor junior teammates, and contribute to project debriefs and team POVs.

Here's What You'll Need

3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, data or platform engineering, or a client-facing technical role such as solutions engineering, technical consulting, or Forward Deployed Engineering. Experience should include hands-on experience building and deploying AI or LLM-powered applications, ideally integrated with real enterprise systems rather than prototypes or demos only.

new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), AWS Forward Deployed Engineering, US Government
new_jobs.description:
Description

Application deadline: Nov 17, 2026

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility or higher.

A Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to independently design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDE IIs write production-grade software and own delivery of complete AI workstreams end-to-end — from requirements gathering through production deployment — combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes.

FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. They design cohesive implementations for ambiguous problems, making design trade-offs with appropriate guidance. They take on projects where the business problem is understood but implementations are not fully fleshed out, balancing constraints and limiting short-term workarounds. They coach others on producing high-quality code and train new team members.

Key job responsibilities

Embed within customer engineering teams. Work with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand the business and customer value of the systems you build. Understand the customer's business processes, technical architecture, and operational constraints. Translate customer requirements into technical designs for AI-enabled production systems within your workstream. Requires 30 – 50% travel.
Build production AI applications. Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.
Own production for your workstream. Be a significant contributor to the full software development lifecycle including scoping, design, code, testing, deployment, operations, and maintenance. Troubleshoot production incidents across AI models, distributed systems, and application services. Ensure root causes of operational issues are identified and resolved. Implement monitoring, evaluations, guardrails, and CI/CD that keep AI systems healthy. Don't settle for the status quo — routinely identify and execute on opportunities to improve operations.
Mentor and uplift. Actively mentors and trains new team members on how systems are constructed, operated, and fit into the bigger picture. Coach others on producing high-quality code through mechanisms such as code review. Be active in the code review process, providing meaningful feedback to others.
Accelerate customer adoption. Identify opportunities to expand AI adoption within your customer engagement. Codify reusable patterns and accelerators that benefit future customer deployments and feed back into AWS services. Make enhancements that improve your team's software and processes.

A day in the life

An FDE II spends the day building inside the customer's environment: pairing with their engineers on production AI features, translating requirements into designs for their workstream, troubleshooting production issues, and reviewing code. They work autonomously on scoped problems, bringing clarity to ambiguous implementations with appropriate guidance from senior FDEs.

About The Team

ABOUT AWS:

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

10047

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
Experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences
Experience with agentic and spec-driven development (developing AI agents a plus)
Experience with AI tools: eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG pipelines, and prompt engineering
Active US Government Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility (or higher)
2+ years of experience working in an Agile, startup, or rapidly scaling environment

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with AWS Services
Experience working in customer production environments
Experience building or deploying AI/ML applications in production environments
Background as a founder, engineering lead, or startup builder with high ownership and urgency
Prior experience with React, TypeScript, Python, and/or Go
Experience interfacing with customers or leading technical projects with external stakeholders

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. new_jobs.title: AI Software Engineer II (Credit)
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are:

NCC is a leader in providing award-winning software, credit and compliance solutions, and cutting-edge data to the automotive industry for over 30 years. Our solutions help dealerships streamline their operations, enhance their finance and insurance (F&I) processes, and drive profitability. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a high-growth environment.

Overview:

We're seeking an AI Software Engineer II
to help build the next generation of AI-powered capabilities. In this role, you'll develop and deliver production-ready software that integrates large language models (LLMs), machine learning, and cloud-based AI services into customer-facing applications.

You'll partner closely with Product and Engineering to rapidly prototype, build, and deploy intelligent features, applying strong software engineering fundamentals to deliver scalable, reliable, and maintainable solutions. This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer with 2–4 years of experience who enjoys solving real-world business problems with modern AI technologies.

What You’ll Do:

Design, build, and deploy AI-powered features within our SaaS platform
Integrate LLMs and cloud AI services into production applications
Develop scalable backend services, REST APIs, and application integrations
Build and maintain data pipelines that support AI workflows
Contribute across the application stack, including backend services and frontend enhancements as needed
Collaborate with Product Managers, UX Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver customer-centric solutions
Rapidly prototype new AI capabilities and iterate on customer feedback
Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code that follows software engineering best practices
Optimize application performance, scalability, and reliability
Participate in code reviews and contribute to architectural decisions

What You’ll Have:

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)
2–4 years of professional software engineering experience
Experience developing applications with Python, C#, Java, JavaScript, or similar object-oriented languages
Experience with consuming or integrating LLMs and AI services via APIs
Experience building RESTful APIs and backend application services
Working knowledge of cloud platforms, including AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud
Experience with Git and modern software development practices
Understanding of databases and data modeling (SQL and/or NoSQL)
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Excellent collaboration and communication skills

Preferred:

Description

Amazon’s third-party marketplace is a multibillion-dollar global ecosystem, connecting customers and sellers across the world through millions of transactions annually. The Seller Fee Science Team integrates economic modeling, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to guide business fee strategy, ensure fees are accurately computed for millions of products, and improves the seller experience with AI tools that support any fee related contact (understanding, audit, and dispute). We build the scientific foundation that empowers sellers to grow their businesses with clarity and confidence.

Our team brings together world-class economists, physicists, mathematicians, and computer scientists to tackle diverse challenging problems that require theoretical rigor and deliver real-world impact. For example, precision measurement of difficult to measure products, large-scale simulation of sales, inventory, and policy changes, as well as leveraging natural language understanding and automated reasoning to interpret policy, generate code, resolve disputes, audit fees, and respond to sellers at meaninful scale.

Your work will shape not only how fees are implemented, but how they are interpreted, experienced, and trusted at scale. You will partner closely with engineers and product partners to take your solutions from research to production.

We are seeking scientists who are motivated by first principles, disciplined experimentation, and the technical challenge of deploying ideas at global scale. This is an opportunity to work on consequential problems where mathematical rigor meets real-world complexity, and where your models, algorithms, and systems will directly influence the experience of millions of sellers. ARCADE is the Science and Analytics team for Amazon Multi-Channel Fulfillment and Commerce (MCCF). ARCADE owns the science behind MCCF's core business decisions. That includes MCF demand forecasting for US and International markets, which feeds capacity planning and OP commitments. It also includes pricing science, from elasticity studies to custom pricing recommendations for enterprise accounts. For Sales and Account Management, we build the merchant retention and propensity models they use to decide which merchants to focus on. We also design and measure experiments for MCCF programs and build models that support ASCS service quality. Each of these runs as a governed mechanism within the business, not a one-off analysis.

In 2027 we're investing into forecasting, measurement and automation. On forecasting, we'll make MCF demand forecasts more accurate and extend regional forecasts to International markets. We'll also build a per-merchant baseline of organic growth. That baseline lets teams measure how much account management actions, product features and discounts actually add, and spot declining merchants early. On automation, we'll automate custom pricing recommendations for enterprise accounts through PRISM. Over the 3-year plan, we'll add cost-to-serve modeling, a supply chain optimizer for inbound placement and routing and a shared framework for monitoring all production models.

NVIDIA played a key role in launching the modern AI era with GPU-accelerated deep learning. Today, generative AI opens outstanding opportunities—helping people share ideas, gain knowledge, and solve problems once out of reach. Making that promise trustworthy is one of the major scientific challenges today. As a Deep Learning Scientist in AI Safety, you will advance research in model alignment, create methods to reduce harmful behaviors, and transform new insights into practical protections for large language models. Join us to develop how advanced AI interacts with people and help extend its benefits worldwide.

NVIDIA is recruiting Senior Deep Learning Scientists to push forward our work in multimodal AI safety, covering Product Security, Content Safety, Bias, and Human-AI Interactions. You will bring core expertise in deep learning to reinforce models for safe reasoning, planning, and acting across different modalities. This opportunity enables you to contribute essential algorithmic advances for foundational models processing diverse data formats. Your initiatives will reach scale via Nemotron Omni platforms, guardrails, and partnerships outside the organization. You will focus on high-impact, prominent safety challenges of large language models and multimodal AI products that improve user experiences for millions. If you are imaginative and driven to tackle real-world agentic AI safety issues, join our team.

What You Will Be Doing

Apply fundamental and applied safety research to develop, train, fine-tune, and deploy large language architectures supporting multimodal agentic reasoning systems and guardrails encompassing text, audio, image, video, and tool usage.
Advance post-training and alignment methods including instruction tuning, preference optimization, and RLHF/RLVR/MOPD to improve safety of multimodal agents for complex use cases.
Research and advance the latest trends in AI safety as applied to pre-/mid-/post-training, guardrails, and steering techniques.
Lead the collection, development, and benchmarking of multimodal safety datasets, ensuring high-quality evaluation of model accuracy, safety, and task completion success.

What We Need To See

Master’s degree (or equivalent experience) or PhD in Computer Science, AI, or Applied Math with 8+ years of relevant work experience.
Excellent programming skills in Python with strong fundamentals in scalable model development and deep learning frameworks like PyTorch.
Strong knowledge of ML/DL techniques and modern foundation model architectures, including Transformers and mixture-of-experts models.
Hands-on experience in post-training multimodal models for multimodal reasoning.
Proven ability to manage model development life cycles, including dataset versioning, experiment tracking, and evaluation pipelines.
Responsible AI Expertise: 1+ years of experience in content safety, ML fairness, AI model security, human-AI interaction, or related areas.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Strong record of publications in top-tier AI and machine learning venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, FAccT, or CVPR.
Experience applying deep reinforcement learning techniques to train multimodal agents in complex simulation.
Safety and Compliance: Proven experience addressing safety and legal and regulatory compliance in multimodal, multilingual, or multi-turn systems.

Experience in at least one of the following risk areas: CBRNE, persuasion and manipulation (influence operations, disinformation, and the erosion of democratic values through AI-generated content), discrimination at scale enabled by AI systems, mental health (sycophancy and manipulation), LLM security (backdoors, data poisoning, latent malicious behavior, structural model vulnerabilities), frontier risks (model deception, manipulation, and loss-of-control scenarios), agentic safety (tool-calling, orchestration, and execution), multi-turn.

new_jobs.description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What You’ll Be Doing...

As a Principal Forward Deployed AI Engineer within Verizon’s Data Analytics team, you will embed directly into the frontline of Verizon’s core Business Units to solve our most critical, ambiguous, and high-stakes operational challenges. Operating with total technical ownership, you will architect, build, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, enterprise RAG engines, full-stack microservices, and decision systems into live operations.

You are a technical anchor: you pair deep systems craftsmanship with a product mindset, cutting through operational ambiguity to design production architectures, implement custom orchestration layers (via LangGraph, Temporal, or custom state machines), and enforce context management strategies that scale into enterprise assets. Beyond shipping point solutions, you will run workloads reliably on Domino, Airflow, and Kubernetes, abstracting bespoke code into reusable SDKs, shared libraries, and architectural playbooks that scale company-wide.

Key Responsibilities Include

End-to-End Architectural Blueprinting: Defining the full-stack architecture for embedded AI initiatives, including multi-agent orchestration, state machines, latency/cost budgets, security boundaries, and enterprise back-end integrations.
Agentic Orchestration Engineering, Workflow Automation and Governance: Architect stateful agent workflows complying with established agentic governance rules, using tools like LangGraph, Temporal, or event-driven state machines, establishing strict protocols for tool calling, execution sandboxing, and deterministic fallback logic.
Context & Retrieval Systems: Designing production RAG infrastructure incorporating hybrid search, re-ranking algorithms, metadata filtering, and semantic caching, directly informing and scaling Verizon’s context architecture.
Runtime & Cloud Deployment: Deploying production agent services and scheduled workflows to target runtimes (e.g., Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes microservices, and serverless compute across AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Evaluation Harness Design: Architecting offline and online evaluation frameworks (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic test generation, human-in-the-loop review queues, live A/B rollouts) to measure model drift, context hallucination rates, and task completion metrics.
Platform Codification & IP Creation: Generalizing custom domain deployments into reusable internal SDKs, API primitives, and modular UI components; mentor engineers across the organization and draft technical documentation for Verizon patent disclosures.
Strategic Discovery & Scoping: Embed alongside BU leadership to map intricate operational processes, cut through organizational noise, and isolate the highest-leverage intervention points where applied AI delivers measurable uplift.
Executive Translation: Serving as the technical authority in the room with BU Vice Presidents and Managing Directors, demystifying algorithmic behaviors, failure modes, and performance trade-offs.

What We’re Looking For...

You’ll need to have:

Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.

You will work closely with recommendation algorithm, growth product and operations, and data science teams to build a high-throughput, low-latency, highly available foundation for personalization at scale, serving more than 80 million users globally. Key Responsibilities

Develop high-throughput, low-latency recommendation services. Continuously improve system performance and reliability, and establish robust degradation and disaster-recovery mechanisms.
Build and optimize large-scale model training infrastructure, including distributed training, job scheduling, resource management, fault recovery, and training observability. Improve training efficiency, stability, and resource utilization.
Build model deployment capabilities and high-performance online inference services. Optimize model loading, inference latency, throughput, and infrastructure cost; implement autoscaling, canary releases, graceful degradation, and disaster recovery to ensure service availability under high traffic.
Establish an engineering feedback loop from offline evaluation and online experimentation to production monitoring. Monitor model quality, service performance, and anomalies; build alerting capabilities to support incident diagnosis and safe rollback.
Collaborate with recommendation algorithm and business engineering teams to identify common needs across trading products, content feeds, community, and other recommendation scenarios. Standardize training, deployment, and inference capabilities to bring models into production reliably and efficiently.

Major Requirements

At least 4 years of recommender systems engineering experience at a consumer-facing internet company. You have contributed substantially to the design and development of a model training platform, model deployment platform, or large-scale online inference service, and have hands-on experience resolving production issues.
Strong computer science fundamentals and proficiency in at least one of Go, Java, or C++. You write well-structured code, apply sound design principles, and enjoy tackling challenging engineering problems.
Familiarity with at least one mainstream deep learning framework, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. You understand the end-to-end workflow of training, exporting, deploying, and serving recommendation models, and have practical experience with distributed training or training job orchestration.
An understanding of the recommendation system lifecycle and the engineering considerations involved in sequence models, multi-objective models, and other recommender model types. Experience designing and optimizing high-throughput, low-latency services. You can diagnose and resolve online inference issues involving throughput, P99 latency, reliability, and resource cost.

Architecture experience in search, advertising, or recommendations at major technology companies
Experience leading the development of a training platform, model deployment platform, or online inference pipeline from the ground up in a large-scale recommendation, advertising, or search system, and making those capabilities reusable across business scenarios.
Experience optimizing distributed training or inference for complex recommendation models, or scheduling heterogeneous CPU/GPU resources.
Experience with cross-region high-availability deployments, active-active architectures, model release governance, or large-scale production incident response.
An AI-driven approach and hands-on experience bringing LLM or agent applications into production for search, advertising, or recommendation use cases.

A multi-domain recommendation challenge in fintech:
Go beyond a single domain such as video or e-commerce. You will build personalization capabilities across trading products, market intelligence, community content, campaigns, and AI-powered investment workflows.

Our combination of trading, content, community, AI, and campaigns creates distinctive technical challenges and enables rapid iteration.
