Description

We are seeking a Forward Deployed Software Engineer to build technology solutions that help public health programs operate more effectively. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys working directly with users, understanding complex operational problems, and turning them into reliable software that delivers measurable value.

As an embedded member of a cross-functional team, you will partner with program staff, technical assistance providers, product teams, engineers, and client stakeholders. You will help uncover needs, shape solutions, build and test them with users, and take successful capabilities into production. The role combines full-stack software engineering, workflow automation, data integration, and applied AI in an environment where requirements evolve as teams learn.

You will be successful if you are equally comfortable writing production code, talking with users, working through ambiguity, and making pragmatic technical decisions.

Responsibilities

Discover and define:
Work directly with program teams, client stakeholders, and end users to understand operational challenges, identify opportunities for technology, and translate loosely defined problems into practical technical solutions.

Prototype and build:
Design and build across the full stack, including user experiences, application services, APIs, relational data models, integrations, workflows, dashboards, and reporting. Move quickly from problem definition to working prototypes and iterate with real user feedback.

Apply AI where it adds value:
Build AI-assisted capabilities such as summarization, structured extraction, classification, and workflow support. Preserve appropriate human review and account for reliability, privacy, data governance, and responsible use.

Deploy and improve:
Move successful capabilities into reliable production environments with maintainability, security, error handling, traceability, testing, and operational support in mind. Observe usage, diagnose issues, and improve solutions based on feedback.

Scale what works:
Turn lessons from program-specific implementations into reusable platform capabilities, technical patterns, and components. Surface gaps between platform capabilities and real-world needs and feed those insights back to product and engineering teams.

Communicate clearly:
Explain technical options, feasibility, tradeoffs, and constraints to technical and non-technical audiences. Support demonstrations, walkthroughs, and hands-on sessions with users and stakeholders.

Qualifications

Required

3 years of professional software engineering experience, including meaningful full-stack development experience.

Additional Qualifications

Strong programming skills and experience building modern web applications with JavaScript/TypeScript or comparable technologies.
Experience with relational databases, APIs, external services, and production software delivery.
Ability to work directly with users and stakeholders to understand problems and translate them into technical solutions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts and tradeoffs to non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated ability to deliver iteratively when requirements are incomplete or changing.
Experience with version control, code review, testing, and collaborative software development practices.

Preferred

Client-facing, embedded, consulting, or Forward Deployed Engineering experience.
Experience integrating LLM capabilities into applications, including summarization, structured extraction, classification, evaluation, or AI-enabled workflows.
Experience building multi-step workflows, stateful applications, or human-in-the-loop processes.
Experience with case management, workflow, grant management, or program management systems.
Cloud-native development, CI/CD, automated testing, observability, or production operations experience.
Experience with government technology environments, sensitive data, data governance, privacy, or responsible AI.
Interest or experience in health, public health, rural health, or public-sector program delivery.
Professional use of AI-assisted software engineering tools.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, users, and real-world operations. You will not simply receive a backlog of fully defined requirements. You will work with stakeholders to understand what they are trying to accomplish, determine the right technical approach, and move from idea to working software. Some problems will require traditional engineering; others may benefit from workflow automation, data integration, or AI.

In your first six months, success means developing a strong understanding of the program and its users, building trusted working relationships, and delivering production capabilities that address meaningful operational needs. Over your first year, you will help turn lessons from individual implementations into reusable capabilities and engineering patterns that make future delivery faster and more consistent.

JavaScript/TypeScript-based front-end development, server-side application development, relational databases, RESTful APIs, cloud services, workflow and state management, LLM-enabled application patterns, version control, CI/CD, and automated testing. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Beneficial Deployments

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

About The Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join Beneficial Deployments, focused on helping nonprofits and foundations get real value from Claude. You'll be the technical lead for a portfolio of partners, working alongside our Account Executives from first conversation through deployment. You'll help partners find where Claude makes a real difference to their mission and their operations, design solutions that fit their budgets, data and teams, and turn early pilots into lasting adoption. What works for one partner becomes something the whole sector can use.

Responsibilities

Serve as the primary technical advisor to a portfolio of nonprofit partners from discovery through deployment, turning their priorities into scoped use cases with clear measures of success.
Partner with Account Executives on account plans, discovery and technical evaluation.
Design and demo solutions with Claude, the API and Claude Code across program delivery, fundraising, operations and data analysis.
Guide partners through security review, data governance and procurement.
Run workshops and trainings that build AI fluency across partner teams.
Build reusable assets (reference designs, connectors, prompt and eval templates) so one partner's work helps the next.
Spot patterns across partners, bring field insight back to Product and Research, and help partners measure what changed.
Travel to partner sites for workshops, technical deep dives and relationship building.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have

3+ years in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering or technical consulting.
A track record of getting lean, skeptical or slow-moving teams to adopt technology and keep using it, including working through how they buy and govern it.
Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you have built and evaluated working prototypes or agents, and can guide a partner's own engineers on architecture and evals. You don't need to write production code.
Clear written and spoken communication across a broad audience. The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to program leads, operations staff and executives.
Patience with long buying cycles, a knack for knowing how to make them go smoothly, and real care for public benefit.
A track record of agency and autonomy: you spot what needs doing before anyone asks, agree that it matters, drive it to a finished result and know when to pull others in.
Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.
Bonus if you've worked in a sales team, or with or at nonprofits, foundations or other mission-driven organizations.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$240,000—$315,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Description

Application deadline: Nov 17, 2026

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility or higher.

A Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to independently design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDE IIs write production-grade software and own delivery of complete AI workstreams end-to-end — from requirements gathering through production deployment — combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes.

FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. They design cohesive implementations for ambiguous problems, making design trade-offs with appropriate guidance. They take on projects where the business problem is understood but implementations are not fully fleshed out, balancing constraints and limiting short-term workarounds. They coach others on producing high-quality code and train new team members.

Key job responsibilities

Embed within customer engineering teams. Work with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand the business and customer value of the systems you build. Understand the customer's business processes, technical architecture, and operational constraints. Translate customer requirements into technical designs for AI-enabled production systems within your workstream. Requires 30 – 50% travel.
Build production AI applications. Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.
Own production for your workstream. Be a significant contributor to the full software development lifecycle including scoping, design, code, testing, deployment, operations, and maintenance. Troubleshoot production incidents across AI models, distributed systems, and application services. Ensure root causes of operational issues are identified and resolved. Implement monitoring, evaluations, guardrails, and CI/CD that keep AI systems healthy. Don't settle for the status quo — routinely identify and execute on opportunities to improve operations.
Mentor and uplift. Actively mentors and trains new team members on how systems are constructed, operated, and fit into the bigger picture. Coach others on producing high-quality code through mechanisms such as code review. Be active in the code review process, providing meaningful feedback to others.
Accelerate customer adoption. Identify opportunities to expand AI adoption within your customer engagement. Codify reusable patterns and accelerators that benefit future customer deployments and feed back into AWS services. Make enhancements that improve your team's software and processes.

An FDE II spends the day building inside the customer's environment: pairing with their engineers on production AI features, translating requirements into designs for their workstream, troubleshooting production issues, and reviewing code. new_jobs.description:
When you join Verizon

You want more out of a career. A place to share your ideas freely — even if they’re daring or different. Where the true you can learn, grow, and thrive. At Verizon, we power and empower how people live, work and play by connecting them to what brings them joy. We do what we love — driving innovation, creativity, and impact in the world. Our V Team is a community of people who anticipate, lead, and believe that listening is where learning begins. In crisis and in celebration, we come together — lifting our communities and building trust in how we show up, everywhere & always. Want in? Join the #VTeamLife.

What You’ll Be Doing...

As a Principal Forward Deployed AI Engineer within Verizon’s Data Analytics team, you will embed directly into the frontline of Verizon’s core Business Units to solve our most critical, ambiguous, and high-stakes operational challenges. Operating with total technical ownership, you will architect, build, and deploy production-grade agentic systems, enterprise RAG engines, full-stack microservices, and decision systems into live operations.

You are a technical anchor: you pair deep systems craftsmanship with a product mindset, cutting through operational ambiguity to design production architectures, implement custom orchestration layers (via LangGraph, Temporal, or custom state machines), and enforce context management strategies that scale into enterprise assets. Beyond shipping point solutions, you will run workloads reliably on Domino, Airflow, and Kubernetes, abstracting bespoke code into reusable SDKs, shared libraries, and architectural playbooks that scale company-wide.

Key Responsibilities Include

End-to-End Architectural Blueprinting: Defining the full-stack architecture for embedded AI initiatives, including multi-agent orchestration, state machines, latency/cost budgets, security boundaries, and enterprise back-end integrations.
Agentic Orchestration Engineering, Workflow Automation and Governance: Architect stateful agent workflows complying with established agentic governance rules, using tools like LangGraph, Temporal, or event-driven state machines, establishing strict protocols for tool calling, execution sandboxing, and deterministic fallback logic.
Context & Retrieval Systems: Designing production RAG infrastructure incorporating hybrid search, re-ranking algorithms, metadata filtering, and semantic caching, directly informing and scaling Verizon’s context architecture.
Runtime & Cloud Deployment: Deploying production agent services and scheduled workflows to target runtimes (e.g., Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes microservices, and serverless compute across AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Evaluation Harness Design: Architecting offline and online evaluation frameworks (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic test generation, human-in-the-loop review queues, live A/B rollouts) to measure model drift, context hallucination rates, and task completion metrics.
Platform Codification & IP Creation: Generalizing custom domain deployments into reusable internal SDKs, API primitives, and modular UI components; mentor engineers across the organization and draft technical documentation for Verizon patent disclosures.
Strategic Discovery & Scoping: Embed alongside BU leadership to map intricate operational processes, cut through organizational noise, and isolate the highest-leverage intervention points where applied AI delivers measurable uplift.
Executive Translation: Serving as the technical authority in the room with BU Vice Presidents and Managing Directors, demystifying algorithmic behaviors, failure modes, and performance trade-offs.

What We’re Looking For...

You’ll need to have:

Bachelor’s degree or four or more years of work experience.
Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
Extensive hands-on experience leveraging frontier LLMs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini) and agentic developer frameworks (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to build scalable solutions and achieve core business milestones.
Experience with containerized deployments (Docker), API design, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
Advanced full-stack programming mastery in Python, SQL, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
Demonstrated ability to independently scope ambiguous technical initiatives and present architectural designs to senior executive stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to interface directly with enterprise stakeholders, translate ambiguous business requirements into technical architectures, and lead project delivery end-to-end.

Even Better If You Have

Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field.
Experience building and scaling centralized context platforms or enterprise search engines similar to Verizon's internal enterprise context layer platforms.
Proven track record implementing both offline evaluation benchmarks and online evaluation/observability pipelines (latency, token costs, hallucination tracking, eval-driven development).
Proven experience deploying containerized services and data workflows across enterprise platforms such as Domino Data Lab, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes (EKS/GKE), and hyperscaler cloud environments (AWS/GCP/Azure).
Proven track record designing offline/online eval harnesses, guardrail frameworks, and observability systems (latency, token optimization, tracing).
Prior forward-deployed engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting experience in top-tier technology firms or hyperscalers.
Record of turning one-off operational builds into enterprise-wide shared libraries, with associated technical publications or filed patents.
Domain knowledge in telecommunications, network capacity optimization, capital planning, or large-scale customer care operations.
Deep expertise in retrieval and context architectures: designing production RAG pipelines, vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Milvus, Pinecone), hybrid search (dense + sparse/lexical), and dynamic context management.

If Verizon and this role sound like a fit for you, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every “even better” qualification listed above.

Where you’ll be working

In this hybrid role, you'll have a defined work location that includes working from home and a minimum of three days per week in the office, which will be set by your manager. Employees are responsible for maintaining compliance with hybrid work policies.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

Equal Employment Opportunity

Verizon is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to veteran status, disability or other legally protected characteristics.

Benefits And Compensation

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of Verizon. From health and wellness benefit options including: medical, dental, vision, short and long term disability, basic life insurance, supplemental life insurance, AD&D insurance, identity theft protection, pet insurance and group home & auto insurance. We also offer a matched 401(k) savings plan, up to 8 company paid holidays per year and up to 6 personal days per year, paid parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition assistance, plus other incentives, we’ve got you covered with our award-winning total rewards package. Depending on the role, employees have the opportunity to receive compensation in the form of premium pay such as overtime, shift differential, holiday pay, allowances, etc. Newly hired employees receive up to 15 days of vacation per year, which grows with additional service. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances.

The salary will vary depending on your location and confirmed job-related skills and experience. This is an incentive based position with the potential to earn more. For part-time roles, your compensation will be adjusted to reflect your hours.

Who We Are Looking For

State Street's Cyber Data & Analytics (CyberDNA) team is seeking a Senior AI Security Automation Engineer to help shape the next generation of cybersecurity data, analytics, and AI-powered platforms. Partnering closely with Global Cyber Security teams, Infrastructure Teams, and Enterprise Continuity Services, this team develops advanced data platforms, intelligent automation solutions, and engineering capabilities that enable cybersecurity teams to make faster, AI-driven decisions and strengthen the firm's ability to detect, prevent, and respond to evolving cyber threats.

Why this role is important to us

Through innovation in AI, analytics, and automation, CyberDNA team plays a critical role in protecting State Street, its clients, and its partners from increasingly sophisticated global threat actors. This role sits at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Engineering, and Full-Stack Software Development, with a primary focus on enabling secure, scalable, and governed AI adoption across the enterprise for supporting Cyber Security functions. The successful candidate will be part of a global AI security automation engineering team focused on delivering next-generation AI platforms, autonomous agents, security automation solutions, and data-driven applications that strengthen cyber resilience, accelerate innovation, and transform cybersecurity operations through intelligent automation.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Senior AI Security Automation Engineer, you will

Drive the architecture and hands-on delivery of scalable, reliable agentic AI platforms for security workflows
Design and build production-grade AI systems including agents, skills, memory patterns, guardrails, and tool-use orchestration
Architect retrieval and context-engineering approaches including embeddings, semantic search, grounding, summarization, and prompt/version management
Engineer cloud-native AI services in AWS, Azure and GCP using containers and serverless patterns, event-driven messaging, and distributed data stores
Optimize platform performance across latency, throughput, scalability, caching, context efficiency, and cost controls
Build well-governed APIs and integrations that connect AI capabilities to security platforms, tools, and business processes
Establish evaluation, research, regression testing, and observability frameworks to continuously improve quality and agent behavior
Define engineering standards for reliability, security, and safe AI operation across the platform lifecycle
Mentor junior engineers and influence engineering direction through code reviews, architecture forums, and cross-team technical leadership
Leverages enterprise-authorized AI coding assist tools within the work environment to improve code quality, delivery speed, and productivity across complex deliverables (e.g., code generation/refactoring, unit test creation, documentation), while validating outputs through peer review, automated testing, and secure coding standards; contributes learnings and reusable patterns to improve broader team effectiveness.
Applies knowledge of tools within the Software Development Life Cycle toolchain, including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development and automation capabilities, to improve the value realized by automation.

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Demonstrated experience architecting, developing, and deploying production-grade Generative AI and Large Language Model (LLM) based solutions, including agentic workflows, intelligent agents, and enterprise tool integration frameworks.
Strong software engineering fundamentals with expertise in designing and delivering cloud-native applications and services leveraging containers, serverless architectures, and modern public cloud platforms.
Proven experience building highly scalable distributed systems utilizing asynchronous processing, event-driven architectures, durable messaging, and high-performance data access patterns.
Hands-on expertise developing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions, including embeddings, semantic search, knowledge grounding, context engineering, prompt optimization, and prompt lifecycle management.
Experience implementing AI evaluation, testing, monitoring, and observability frameworks to measure model quality, reliability, performance, and safe operation in production environments.
Strong API design and integration experience, including the development of secure, reusable, and scalable platform services that enable enterprise-wide adoption of AI capabilities.
Demonstrated technical leadership skills with a track record of mentoring engineers, driving architectural decisions, influencing technology strategy, and collaborating effectively with cross-functional stakeholders.
Hands-on experience utilizing enterprise-approved AI-assisted software development tools to accelerate application delivery, improve code quality, streamline testing, and enhance documentation, while ensuring outputs are validated through secure coding practices, peer review, and automated testing.
Strong understanding of responsible AI principles, including data privacy, security, governance, resiliency, and risk management, with the ability to guide teams in the safe and effective use of AI technologies.
Deep understanding of cybersecurity data sources, including endpoint, network, application, cloud, and system telemetry, and their application in security monitoring, analytics, and automation.
Experience working with Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms and cybersecurity analytics solutions to ingest, correlate, retrieve, and analyze large-scale security data.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity operations, including threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, security analytics, and security automation.
Proven ability to lead and influence geographically distributed teams through virtual collaboration, fostering strong partnerships, driving technical outcomes, and building effective relationships across engineering, security, and business organizations.
Deep understanding of CI/CD tools (Jenkins, Harness, Spinnaker, Argo CD, etc.) and methodology, production experience in designing and implementing CI/CD pipelines with a focus on helping teams release frequently to production while maintaining deployment reliability
Strong software development and automation skills with demonstrated experience in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go (Golang), Bash, and PowerShell.
Proven ability to lead complex technical initiatives while remaining deeply hands-on.
Experience developing cybersecurity, analytics, or operational intelligence solutions.
Proven ability to lead complex technical initiatives while remaining deeply hands-on.
LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, AutoGen, LangChain, or similar frameworks.
Databricks, Snowflake, Spark, Kafka, Delta Lake, Iceberg, and Airflow.
Experience with vector databases, semantic search, and enterprise RAG platforms.
Experience implementing MLOps, LLMOps, AI observability, and evaluation frameworks.
Knowledge of Responsible AI, data governance, and model risk management.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

Master’s or bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline.
7+ years of professional software engineering experience.
3+ years of experience developing AI, Machine Learning, or Generative AI solutions.
Demonstrated success designing and deploying enterprise-scale applications and platforms.
Experience developing cybersecurity, analytics, or operational intelligence solutions.

Work Requirement

Work shift is 8 AM – 5 PM local time with occasional Level 2-3 escalation resolution to support operational incidents
This hybrid role includes an in-office presence requirement of 2–4 days per week, consistent with the organization's hybrid work policy.

The Opportunity

About The Role

The Sr. MLOps Engineer treats ML systems as software systems and owns the path from a trained model to a production endpoint that meets its latency, cost, and reliability budgets — across both batch scoring (SageMaker Batch Transform, Snowflake Cortex / Snowpark ML, dbt-orchestrated scoring) and real-time inference (SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock, sub-second feature serving). The Sr. Engineer builds the platform that data scientists and ML engineers ship on: feature store with guaranteed online/offline parity, model registry, CI/CD for ML, drift and quality monitoring, champion/challenger and shadow deployment scaffolding. This requires a software-engineering-first mindset — distributed systems, observability, and on-call instincts are the foundation; ML literacy makes them effective for this role. GenAI integration experience is a plus, not a requirement.

Responsibilities

ML Production Platform
Stand up and operate BetMGM's ML platform on AWS (SageMaker Training, Model Registry, Pipelines, Endpoints, Batch Transform) and Snowflake (Snowpark ML, Cortex), with Terraform-managed infrastructure
Build self-service scaffolds that let data scientists ship a model end-to-end without a ticket queue — cookie-cutter project templates with CI, drift monitoring, alerting, IaC, and Snowflake connectivity pre-baked

Batch and Real-Time Inference
Design and operate batch scoring pipelines — SageMaker Batch Transform, dbt-orchestrated scoring against Snowflake, Snowpark ML — with explicit freshness and cost SLAs.
Design and operate real-time inference paths — SageMaker real-time endpoints, Lambda + Bedrock for GenAI, API Gateway — with stated latency budgets (typically sub-100ms) and graceful degradation under load.
Own the feature store (SageMaker Feature Store, Tecton, or Feast) with guaranteed online/offline parity — training-serving skew is treated as an incident, not a tradeoff.

CI/CD and Deployment Patterns
Build CI/CD for ML — model registry, automated retraining triggers, model versioning, lineage from feature → training run → deployed model → live prediction.
Implement champion/challenger, shadow deployments, and canary releases as platform primitives so individual model teams do not reinvent them per project.

Monitoring, Drift & Reliability
Stand up drift detection, data quality, and model performance monitoring (Evidently, Arize, or SageMaker Model Monitor — pick one and standardize) with paging that routes to humans who can fix it.
Own MLOps incident response — production model failures are SEV events with postmortems.

Cost and Performance
Right-size endpoints, batch caching, request batching, and autoscaling. State cost-per-prediction targets up front and meet them.

GenAI Integration (Plus, Not Required)
Integrate LLM APIs (Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI) into production paths — RAG pipelines, agent eval frameworks, prompt versioning, cost and latency observability.
Partner with the Helix team on AI personalization workloads as they ramp toward March Madness 2027.
undefined

Direct AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, dbt Copilot) as a force multiplier across infrastructure code, eval suites, and model-serving glue — designing work for agents to do, not just accepting their suggestions.

Partner with the data engineering team on shared standards (Terraform modules, CI/CD patterns, observability, lineage).
Work alongside data scientists and analytics partners to land the right interfaces between research and production — opinionated about the boundary.
Coordinate with Entain India and contractor ML partners as workloads consolidate onto the BetMGM-owned platform.

5+ years shipping software in production — Python, Docker, Kubernetes or ECS, CI/CD, distributed systems debugging — including time on-call.
3+ years operating ML in production — you have owned a model in prod that served real traffic, with stated latency and cost budgets and a runbook you wrote.
AWS depth across the SageMaker surface (Training, Endpoints, Batch Transform, Model Registry, Pipelines) plus the supporting cast (IAM, Lambda, ECS, S3, Secrets Manager, VPC).
Snowflake fluency — Snowpark ML, Cortex, dbt-orchestrated batch scoring, RBAC for ML workloads.
IaC for ML — Terraform + SageMaker Pipelines or equivalent. No manual console deployments to production.
Feature store experience — SageMaker Feature Store, Tecton, or Feast — with explicit ownership of online/offline parity.
Champion/challenger, shadow, and canary deployment patterns as production muscle, not blog-post familiarity.
Drift and model monitoring — Evidently, Arize, WhyLabs, or SageMaker Model Monitor — wired to a paging path.
Software-engineering-first mindset — you treat ML systems as systems, not notebooks.
Nice-to-Haves
GenAI in production — Bedrock, Anthropic, or OpenAI APIs integrated into live systems; RAG pipelines; vector DBs (Snowflake Cortex Search, pgvector, Pinecone); evaluation frameworks (Langfuse or in-house).
Snowflake-native ML — Snowpark Container Services, Cortex AISQL, Cortex Agents — for workloads that do not need to leave the warehouse.
Streaming feature engineering — Kafka, Flink, or Snowpipe Streaming — for sub-second features.
Fine-tuning experience — LoRA, QLoRA, instruction tuning, eval-driven iteration — with an honest read on when fine-tuning beats prompting.
A track record of shipping more with AI in the engineering loop than without.
Regulated-industry experience (gaming, fintech, healthcare) — comfort with model risk, audit, and lineage requirements.

Description

AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

On Agentic WorkSpaces, our vision is to enable AI agents to work the way humans do — with access to real applications, real interfaces, and real computing environments. We're building foundational infrastructure that allows autonomous agents to securely provision, interact with, and manage computing sessions at scale. Our work sits at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, agentic AI, and security, and directly shapes how the next generation of AI agents will operate in enterprise environments.

We are seeking an exceptional Senior SDE to help build the systems that make this possible. This is an early role on a new team working on problems that do not have established patterns. You will own the architecture of distributed systems that let AI agents access real computing environments, spin up and tear down sessions at unpredictable scale, and operate reliably across platforms our customers already depend on. You will write code, make foundational architectural decisions, mentor and grow the engineers around you, and partner with senior technical leaders across the organization. This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role on a small team solving hard problems with no established playbook. If you do your best work in ambiguity and want your technical decisions to set the direction for an emerging product category, this team is for you.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end technical architecture for distributed systems at enterprise scale
Lead cross-platform expansions of core capabilities
Evaluate build-vs-leverage decisions for infrastructure primitives, including assessments of existing internal and external components for reuse
Drive technical consensus across partner teams with competing priorities and constraints
Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews and design reviews
Communicate architectural decisions and tradeoffs to senior leadership and non-technical stakeholders

A day in the life

Your mornings are usually free for focus work - architecture deep dives and hard problems. Around 11 you'll have standup then grab lunch with the team (if you like) before the afternoon opens up for design reviews CR feedback or unblocking an engineer. Some days you're deep in code; others you're presenting to leadership. You're the person who knows the system most deeply - and you work to ensure you're never the bottleneck. The problems are hard and the stakes are high - but we believe we can move fast do exceptional work and have a full life outside of it.

Job Title
: Principal AI Cloud Architect – Azure Cloud

Location:
US (Remote)

Employment Type:
Full-time

Job Description

We are seeking a seasoned Principal AI Cloud Architect to lead the shift of our Cloud business unit to an AI-first operating model. This role will build and lead a small team of engineers focused on designing, deploying, and running AI agents that manage, monitor, and optimize our Cloud infrastructure in Microsoft Azure. It is also client-facing. You will help clients adopt AI-driven Cloud operations and work closely with development teams to deliver enterprise-grade solutions.

The ideal candidate is an expert in Azure architecture with hands-on experience building production agentic AI systems. They also bring deep knowledge of data platforms (including Databricks), Cloud networking, identity and access management, and operational excellence. They will set the AI strategy for the Cloud business unit and turn it into working agents that reduce manual effort, improve reliability, and keep Cloud environments secure, compliant, and cost-effective.

Key Responsibiliti
es

Define and drive the AI strategy and roadmap for the Cloud business unit, moving infrastructure operations from manual and script-based processes to agent-driven automation
Build, lead, and mentor a team of 2–6 AI and Cloud engineers responsible for designing, developing, and operating AI agents in production
Architect multi-agent systems for AIOps, including anomaly detection, event correlation, ITSM ticket triage, and self-healing runbooks that reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR)
Lead the design of agents that generate, review, and validate Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Bicep), with policy checks and automated validation built into CI/CD pipelines before changes reach production
Develop FinOps agents that identify cost anomalies, rightsizing opportunities, and idle resources, and act on them within defined guardrails
Design security and compliance agents for posture assessment, configuration drift detection, and automated collection of audit evidence
Establish AI governance for agent operations, including human-in-the-loop approvals, access controls, guardrails, audit logging, and responsible AI practices suited to a regulated healthcare environment
Partner with business stakeholders, clients, and engineering teams to define and architect end-to-end Cloud and AI solutions aligned with strategic objectives
Lead architecture for data and analytics platforms, including Azure Databricks and the data foundations that support AI workloads
Drive operational excellence, including monitoring, logging, observability, resiliency, and disaster recovery, for both Cloud platforms and the agents that run on them
Establish and promote architecture standards, reusable agent patterns, and reference architectures across the organization
Translate complex technical concepts into clear business value for clients and executive stakeholders, including measurable outcomes from AI adoption
Evaluate emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and models, and keep improving the organization’s Cloud and AI capabilities and innovation roadmap

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Leads and executes deep dive diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to support data-driven business decision making. Mentors and develops junior data scientists and analysts.

Vanguard is committed to continuous Client Experience improvement, and the Enterprise Intelligence group develops and supports a suite of internal CX analytical tools. These Data Science tools – spanning models, software, and interfaces – are used by internal Vanguard expert analysts to better understand CX outcomes. This position is for a full stack Data Scientist supporting the continued development of our internal suite of CX analytical tools. The role will be responsible for rapidly understanding the current state of those methods / models / systems, then working with existing Data Science and Machine Learning stakeholders to support and update that suite.

Applicants should have a baseline understanding of the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), deployment of code through Python packages, integration of AI into code (both in development and application), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) fundamentals for text processing & analysis. Your work will connect with subject matter experts across Data Science, Analytics, Client Experience, and Business – you’ll need to be able to cater your technical communication across audiences. You will follow the Vanguard Model Governance process and adhere to AI usage policies, protecting client information and ensuring full compliance with safety & security best practices.

You’ll be working with a highly-skilled team of Data Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers, on a suite of software that has moved beyond its initial development stages. This will demand rapid familiarization, the ability to quickly understand existing codebase, and finding opportunities for improvement. You will need to work with your management and stakeholders to prioritize tasking, autonomously deliver on that tasking, and proactively come back with proposed next steps.

Core Responsibilities

Deliver technology:

Build and support existing software, models, packages, and other analytics tools used for data-driven business decision making.
Implement AI prompt engineering, NLP text processing, and unstructured data modeling in systems & packages.
Deploy software to internal consumers, adhere to the PDLC process, create and use monitoring & tracking features.

Use technology responsibly:

Follow the Vanguard Model Governance methodology & process, adhering to security policies around AI usage, software design, and model validation.
Identify and diagnose data & code issues, always through continuous code review, and when necessary by performing root-cause analysis and post-mortems.
Proactively surface found issues or risks.

Manage stakeholders:

Engage with internal stakeholders (DS, MLE, Business...) to understand and probe business processes in order to improve CX models, packages, and tools.
Establish Definitions-of-Done with stakeholders, ensure that DoD is tracked and met through the PDLC process.
Communicate complex findings and implications to leaders & teammates.

Be a team player:

Mentor and develop junior data scientists and analysts.
Actively share information across workstreams, promote cross-pollination of findings & hurdles.
Participate in special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of five years related work experience in Data Science development & modeling roles.
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or related Data Science field of study, or equivalent combination of training and experience. Graduate degree preferred.
Experience with the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), especially deploying Data Science tools to expert analyst users.
Proven experience using AI and NLP methods & tools to extract information from unstructured data at scale. Strong background using quantified measures to evaluate text, developing models around those measures, and improving them over time.
Advanced programming experience with Python, including deploying solutions as Packages that include telemetry feedback, safeguards, secure credentialing, and other User Access Controls (UAC).
Ability to communicate technically complex concepts across varying audiences. Know when to dive deep, and when to keep things high-level.
Some experience with data wrangling required – ability to extract, transform and load (ETL) large-scale data for statistical modeling.
Preference for candidates who have worked with Client Experience & client outcomes, who have familiarity with terminology surrounding client feedback & stories.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

new_jobs.title: Research Scientist: NLP & NLU
new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Founded in Santa Barbara in 2003, AIMdyn, Inc. is a woman-owned small business developing predictive modeling, artificial intelligence, and world-modeling technologies for large-scale complex engineering, natural science, and social science problems. AIMdyn supports government, commercial, and academic customers, including DARPA, the Air Force Office of Scientific Research, and the Office of Naval Research. Visit aimdyn.com to learn more

Research Scientist: NLP & NLU

AIMdyn, Inc. is seeking a Research Scientist with expertise in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Natural Language Understanding (NLU), and machine learning to develop language-based classification and decision-support capabilities for advanced research programs.
The successful candidate will develop methods for extracting structured, actionable information from specialized natural-language inputs. The initial research will emphasize classification and representation of domain-specific language, including identifying operational categories, intent, preferences, constraints, and other latent information contained in natural-language statements.
This position is intended for a researcher with substantive NLP expertise rather than primarily prompt-engineering or application-level experience with large language models. The candidate will investigate and implement appropriate approaches spanning conventional NLP, transformer-based models, embedding and representation learning, fine-tuned language models, and other modern machine-learning techniques.
The successful candidate will work closely with AIMdyn researchers in machine learning, uncertainty quantification, dynamical systems, and decision science to incorporate natural-language information into larger analytical and decision-support systems.

Responsibilities

Research, develop, implement, and evaluate natural-language classification and understanding methods.
Develop classifiers for specialized domain language, including multiclass, multilabel, hierarchical, and structured classification problems as appropriate.
Develop representations of natural-language statements using transformer models, embeddings, representation learning, or other NLP techniques.
Extract structured information such as intent, preferences, constraints, entities, relationships, and operational concepts from free-form text.
Investigate approaches appropriate for small or specialized labeled datasets, including transfer learning, few-shot learning, weak supervision, semi-supervised learning, active learning, and synthetic-data generation.
Develop and evaluate fine-tuning and adaptation strategies for pretrained language models.
Establish rigorous evaluation methodologies, datasets, benchmarks, and error-analysis processes for language models and classifiers.
Evaluate classifier calibration, uncertainty, ambiguity, robustness, and performance under distribution or domain shift.
Investigate out-of-distribution detection and methods for identifying inputs that cannot be classified reliably.
Work with domain experts to develop labeling schemes, taxonomies, ontologies, and annotation procedures for specialized language.
Develop reusable research software and integrate NLP capabilities into larger analytical software systems.
Clearly communicate model behavior, assumptions, limitations, experimental results, and research findings to interdisciplinary teams.

Education Requirements

M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Statistics, or a closely related technical field.

Required Technical Expertise

Demonstrated research or applied experience in natural language processing or natural language understanding.
Strong understanding of modern NLP methods, including transformer architectures, contextual representations, embeddings, and supervised language-model adaptation.
Experience developing and evaluating text-classification systems.
Strong Python programming skills and hands-on experience with modern machine-learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
Experience with common NLP ecosystems such as Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence Transformers, spaCy, or comparable tools.
Strong research, analytical, and technical communication skills.
Strong technical communication and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience fine-tuning or adapting transformer-based language models and large language models.
Experience with representation learning and embedding-based approaches for semantic classification.
Experience constructing annotation guidelines, taxonomies, ontologies, or labeled NLP datasets.
Strong publication record or demonstrated independent research in NLP, machine learning, or related areas.
Familiarity with Koopman operator methods or related operator-theoretic approaches to dynamical systems.

Additional Qualifications

Strong independent research and problem-solving ability.
Ability to communicate model limitations, ambiguity, uncertainty, and failure modes clearly.
Ability to collaborate with researchers from disciplines outside NLP and translate domain requirements into technical machine-learning problems.

Compensation & Benefits

Research Scientist: $53.93 - $57.21 / Hr
Generous Health & Welfare program
401(k) retirement program

Location & Citizenship

U.S. location only; work abroad is not permitted due to contract restrictions. Remote work may be authorized. U.S. citizenship is required for this role due to requirements of some government projects (this is not a general company policy or requirement).
Candidates in California central coast (Ventura/Santa Barbara county) and Minneapolis are preferred but not required.

Job Profile

Position Overview

At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. As a Data Scientist Lead within PNC's Data, Modeling & Analytics Home Lending organization, you will be based in Pittsburgh, PA, Tysons Corner, VA or East Brunswick, NJ.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Hands-on experience designing agentic LLM workflows (Azure AI Foundry/OpenAI), propensity and ML modeling, and backtesting at scale

Strong Python/SQL/PySpark

Home Lending or retail banking domain knowledge

Experience with prompt governance, responsible AI, and model validation

Proven ability to lead data science teams and deliver production AI solutions to business users

PNC is an in-office company that fosters a supportive culture where employees can thrive and achieve balance. We encourage candidates to connect with their recruiter and hiring manager to understand workplace expectations and ensure the role aligns with their goals.

PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position.

Job Description

Directs and consults on analytical projects that leverage vast amounts of structured and unstructured data to extract actionable business insights.
Directs the data gathering, data processing and data mining of large and complex datasets. Provides deep technical expertise to advance the data science capabilities of analytics teams.
Serves as a representative of PNC; understands the needs and challenges PNC is facing and provides thought leadership around data science activities both internally and externally.
Supervises the implementation of advanced analytics projects, and as an expert in the field, helps other data scientists present the analytical processes and outcomes to management.
Partners with Data Architects, Data Analysts, Data Engineers and Visualization Experts to develop data-driven solutions for the business.

PNC Employees take pride in our reputation and to continue building upon that we expect our employees to be:

Customer Focused - Knowledgeable of the values and practices that align customer needs and satisfaction as primary considerations in all business decisions and able to leverage that information in creating customized customer solutions.
Managing Risk - Assessing and effectively managing all of the risks associated with their business objectives and activities to ensure they adhere to and support PNC's Enterprise Risk Management Framework.

Qualifications

Successful candidates must demonstrate appropriate knowledge, skills, and abilities for a role. Listed below are skills, competencies, work experience, education, and required certifications/licensures needed to be successful in this position.

Preferred Skills

Analytical Thinking, Competitive Advantages, Data Analytics, Data Mining, Data Science, Machine Learning (ML)

Data Architecture, Data Mining, Disruptive Innovation, Information Capture, Machine Learning, Modeling: Data, Process, Events, Objects, Prototyping, Query and Database Access Tools

new_jobs.title: Principal Data Scientist - Experimentation & Causal Inference
new_jobs.description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Data Scientist - Experimentation & Causal Inference
to serve as the statistical brain behind our rapidly growing experimentation program. You will own the methodology layer that ensures every experiment we run is trustworthy, sensitive, and correctly interpreted.
You will NOT be building infrastructure or writing backend services — our platform engineering team handles that. Your job is to design, validate, and continuously improve the statistical frameworks that sit on top of the platform. You will be the person the team turns to when they ask "Can we trust this result?" — and you will build the automated systems that answer that question before anyone needs to ask.
Team context:
You will join a team of data scientists and platform engineers within the Big Data group, reporting to the Head of Big Data. The experimentation platform engineering team implements your specifications into production systems.

Responsibility

Guardrail Metrics & SRM Detection

Design and maintain automated anomaly detection for live experiments — including Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) checks and traffic split validation.
Define alerting thresholds and circuit-breaking criteria so compromised experiments are flagged or stopped before polluting decisions.
Define and validate guardrail metrics (sensitivity, directionality, interpretability) that protect the business during every experiment.

Variance Reduction & Sensitivity

Implement and iterate on CUPED and related pre-experiment covariate adjustment methods to reduce metric variance.
Develop techniques to remove noise from user historical behavior, enabling faster detection of true treatment effects — especially in limited-traffic or high-priority scenarios.
Example of impact we are targeting:
Shorten average experiment duration from 14 days to 9 days, unlocking 40%+ more experiments per quarter.

Continuous A/A Experiment Monitoring

Design and run continuous A/A experiments as an always-on health check for the data pipeline (from client-side event reporting through message queues to the real-time data warehouse).
Monitor metric baseline volatility and pipeline stability, ensuring the instrumentation layer remains trustworthy over time. You define what "healthy" looks like; the platform team implements the monitoring infrastructure.

Other responsibilities

Partner with product, engineering, and growth teams on experiment design: sample size calculations, metric selection, duration estimation, and result interpretation. Advise on causal inference methods (DID, synthetic control, RDD) when randomization is not feasible.
Translate your methods into specifications, validation scripts, and decision frameworks that the team can operationalize — enabling experiment owners to self-serve while maintaining rigor.

Requirements

Education:
MS or PhD in Statistics, Biostatistics, Economics (Econometrics), Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.
Experience:
5+ years of industry experience designing and analyzing online controlled experiments at a tech company with meaningful user scale (not exclusively survey experiments or clinical trials).
Core Statistical Knowledge:
Solid foundations in hypothesis testing, power analysis, multiple testing correction, and sequential testing. Hands-on experience with at least two of: variance reduction methods (CUPED or similar), sample ratio mismatch detection, or continuous data quality monitoring for experiments.
Programming:
Proficient in Python (scipy, statsmodels, or equivalent) for statistical analysis and simulation. Comfortable writing complex SQL (window functions, CTEs) for data extraction and validation.
Communication & Collaboration:
Ability to explain complex statistical concepts to non-technical stakeholders, translate business questions into rigorous experimental designs, and define clear specifications so engineers can implement your methods in production.
AI-Native Workflow:
Strong AI Sense — extensive hands-on experience with AI coding tools (Claude Code, OpenClaw, or similar). Demonstrated ability to leverage AI assistants to automate repetitive analytical tasks, accelerate code development, and build self-serve tooling faster. You treat AI tools as a daily productivity multiplier, not a novelty.

new_jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer, Human Physiology Modeling
new_jobs.description:
We create a place where people can grow, be their best, be safe, and feel welcome, valued and included. We offer a competitive salary, an annual bonus based on company performance, healthcare and wellbeing programs, pension plan membership, and shares and savings programme. We embrace modern work practices; our Performance with Choice programme offers a remote or hybrid working model, empowering you to find the optimal balance between remote and in-office work.

Discover more about our company-wide benefits and life at GSK on our webpage Life at GSK | GSK

Find out more about GSK and R&D: Our approach to R&D

Senior AI/ML Engineer, Human Physiology Modeling

GSK is building a computational capability that models human physiology as an interconnected, multiscale system. We are hiring the founding member of a new team. You will set the technical direction, build the first models and help define the team's practices.

You will also connect models across scales, from molecular and cellular to tissue, organ and whole-body level and turn that scope into a prioritized modeling roadmap, choosing the right method for each question. You will work with key stakeholders across GSK. The goal is models that inform real decisions, such as target hypotheses, mechanism of action, safety, biomarkers and patient stratification.

This is a hands-on role. You will write, review and ship production-quality scientific software, as well as set the scientific direction.

This is a hybrid role in the United States in San Francisco, CA or Cambridge, MA. You will be expected to work on-site regularly and collaborate with colleagues across sites and regions in the United States.

This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following
:

Define and own the modeling strategy and phased roadmap across the team's organ systems. Recommend sequencing based on scientific tractability, data availability and portfolio relevance.
Build, calibrate and validate multiscale models of physiological function, regulation and disease.
Define how models of different organ systems and scales interface and compose.
Integrate heterogeneous data into models: human genetics and genomics, single-cell and spatial omics, imaging, clinical and EHR data, and published physiology knowledge.
Establish standards for uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, parameter identifiability and model validation.
Write reproducible, tested, version-controlled and containerized code that runs on GSK cloud and HPC infrastructure, in partnership with platform engineering.
Work with experimental colleagues to design studies that test or constrain model predictions.
Communicate results and their limits clearly to scientists and senior leaders.
Help hire, onboard and mentor future team members. Evangelize and enforce code-review, documentation and modeling standards set by the group.
Track the external literature and open-source ecosystem, and contribute or publish where appropriate.

Basic Qualifications:

We are looking for professionals with these required skills to achieve our goals:

A minimum of a BS, MS, or PhD in computational or systems biology, biomedical engineering, physics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field.
A minimum of 4 years of experience with a PhD, a minimum of 5 years of experience with an MS and a minimum of 8 years of experience with a BS. All experience must involve building and applying quantitative models of biological or physiological systems, in academia or industry. For candidates without an advanced degree, a track record of published work, shipped models or open-source contributions can substitute for some of the required years.
A minimum of 2 years of experience modeling the physical and biological processes that recur across organ systems. These include fluid flow and transport, mass exchange across barriers and membranes, tissue mechanics, hormonal and neural regulation, and cell population dynamics.
A minimum of 4 years of experience with Advanced Python Programming. You can write robust, tested, maintainable scientific code using version control, CI/CD and containerization.
A minimum of 2 years of modeling human physiology.
A minimum of 2 years of taking models from concept to a result that changed a scientific or program decision.

Preferred Qualifications:

Please note the following skills are not necessary, just preferred, if you do not have them, please still apply:

Experience with organ-level or whole-body modeling, including physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) and quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models.
Familiarity with open-source simulation tools and standards (for example PhysiCell, COPASI, OpenCOR, FEniCS, SBML and CellML) and with HPC/GPU workflows.
Experience with differentiable simulation, physics-informed ML, learned world models or generative models of biological systems. Experience with LLM and agentic tooling for scientific workflows is also useful.
Experience with Kubernetes, workflow orchestration and MLOps on cloud or HPC.
Publications in computational biology, systems biology or ML venues, or open-source contributions.
Experience mentoring or technically leading small teams.

Skills

Artificial Intelligence (AI), Artificial Intelligence Ethics, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNS), Classification Models, Deep Learning, Intelligent Automation (IA), Machine Learning (ML), Model Evaluation, Model Validation, Predictive Modeling, Probabilistic Modeling, Python (Programming Language), Test Documentation

If you are based in Cambridge, MA; Waltham, MA; Rockville, MD; or San Francisco, CA, the annual base salary for new hires in this position ranges $160,050 to $266,750. The US salary ranges take into account a number of factors including work location within the US market, the candidate’s skills, experience, education level and the market rate for the role. In addition, this position offers an annual bonus and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program which is dependent on the level of the role. Available benefits include health care and other insurance benefits (for employee and family), retirement benefits, paid holidays, vacation, and paid caregiver/parental and medical leave. If salary ranges are not displayed in the job posting for a specific country, the relevant compensation will be discussed during the recruitment process.

Please visit GSK US Benefits Summary to learn more about the comprehensive benefits program GSK offers US employees.

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

You will be a trusted technical advisor to our OEM partners and their customers, turning the NVIDIA AI software stack into validated, deployable solutions for generative AI and large language models. Would you like to join us at the forefront of enterprise AI?

Partner with NVIDIA’s OEM partners to define, validate, and document enterprise AI solutions built on the NVIDIA AI software stack.
Architect and deliver customer proof-of-concepts and custom demos that show generative AI solving critical business problems, from RAG-based assistants to fine-tuned models.
Act as the OEM team’s technical authority on NVIDIA AI software, troubleshooting deployments from CUDA and container runtimes through model serving and distributed inference.
Enable OEM and channel technologists on joint NVIDIA and OEM AI solutions through training, workshops, and sessions at industry events.
Bring field insight from customer deployments back to NVIDIA product and engineering teams to shape future releases.

8+ years as a solutions architect, software engineer, or in a technical presales role, and a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Proven experience designing and deploying production AI software for enterprise customers, including model serving, MLOps pipelines, and Kubernetes-based orchestration.
Hands-on experience building and deploying generative AI applications, including LLM inference, fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
Strong Python programming skills for building AI applications, APIs, and automation.
Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to explain complex technical topics to non-experts.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with NVIDIA AI software, such as NVIDIA NIM, NVIDIA NeMo Framework, Nemotron models, Dynamo, NVIDIA Triton Inference Server, TensorRT, TensorRT-LLM
Experience developing validated AI solution designs with an OEM or system integrator.
Experience with MLOps and AI workload orchestration platforms, such as NVIDIA Run:ai.
Experience benchmarking and optimizing AI inference performance, such as MLPerf Inference.
Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you are creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you!
